# Game design search — "head-tracked catch falling hats AR game santa christmas"

Ranked 6 mechanics. Each mechanic carries any of: **buildables** (DSL scaffolds you can apply via `apply_template`) and **visual references** (curated themes / concept art for borrowing layout, palette, framing).

**Decision guide (two tiers)**:
- **strong** (cosine ≥ 0.50) — a serious candidate. APPLY its buildable via `apply_template` ONLY if your design's gameplay loop, win/lose, AND primary input all match it — then adapt theme / assets / params on top. If the core mechanic diverges (you'd rip out its defining behaviour), do NOT apply: build your own and borrow specific elements / visuals instead.
- **weak** (cosine ≥ 0.30) — loosely related. Do NOT apply; borrow individual visual elements / layout / palette only.
- **Borrowing** (either tier): record what you took via `mechanic_refs: [{mechanic_id, borrowed_elements: [...]}]`. `mechanic_id` is the MECHANIC heading id (the id in backticks next to each **bold** mechanic name below) — NOT a buildable id; buildable ids go only in `starter_template.template_id`. Each borrowed element must be reflected in your plan's assets[]/screens[]/interactions[]/criteria[].


## Strong-tier matches [tier: strong]

Serious candidates. A buildable here is an `apply_template` candidate — but ONLY if your design's gameplay loop, win/lose, AND primary input all match it. If the core mechanic diverges, build your own and borrow elements / visuals instead (applying a half-fit scaffold leaves the wrong core mechanic to patch around).

- **Chef Hat Catch** (`chef_hat_catch`) — score 0.507
  - family: head-tracked-catch
  - gameplay: Cartoon food ingredients fall from the top of the screen at random horizontal positions, intermixed with occasional burnt/bad items to dodge. Player drags (or moves head/face horizontally) a cooking pot along the bottom to catch the good ingredients and avoid the bad ones. Each good catch increments the score; bad catches deduct points or end a streak. Round is time-limited; goal is a high score before the timer expires.
  - tags: catch, falling, drag, swipe, head, face, camera, ingredients, pot, avoid, score, speech_bubble, casual
  - **visual reference** `chef_hat_catch_concept` — Chef Hat Catch concept
    - description: Head-tracked catch in cooking theme: small chef-character sticker beside the head, blue cooking pot at bottom-center, ingredients (tomato/egg/noodles) + burnt-bad items falling from top.
    - concept images: concept (attached above when within the image cap — match them by the numbered legend)

## Weak-tier matches [tier: weak]

Loosely related. Do not apply. Borrow individual visual elements / layout / palette via `mechanic_refs` if any fit.

- **Send gift to friend** (`send_gift_to_friend`) — score 0.444
  - family: Precision/2D Drop
  - gameplay: Santa gift-delivery: a Santa figure swings horizontally on a rope at the top of the screen carrying 3 gifts. Player taps to release the current gift; it falls straight down from Santa's instantaneous x position. 3 houses with chimney chutes (BoxCollider2D walls + HouseFloor delivery zone) sit at the bottom — each with a Profile Photo friend on the roof. Land the gift inside a chimney = delivery success; misses bounce off the roof. Score = total successful deliveries across 3 gift releases. Christmas themed.
  - tags: drop, physics, gift, friend, social, christmas, santa, swing, chimney, house, delivery, precision
  - **buildable** `send_gift_to_friend`
    - description: 2D physics gift-delivery game: Santa swings on a rope at the top, carrying 3 gifts in his arms. Player taps to release a gift; it falls straight down from Santa's current x position. Each of 3 houses has a chimney chute (BoxCollider2D walls + HouseFloor delivery zone) and a Profile Photo friend on the front porch. Gift entering a chimney chute lands on the HouseFloor → that friend is marked delivered, a green check appears above the chimney. Game ends after all 3 gifts thrown: 'Success!' if all friends got a gift, 'Failed!' otherwise. Mirrors the reference Give-Gift-to-Friend project; gifts stay parented to Santa for free swing-along behavior, RigidBody2D physics overrides the parent transform on release. Social Kit Profile Photo placeholders show colored circles in the editor; real friend photos appear after publication. The template ships with primitive-shape placeholders for Santa, houses, gifts, and trees — after applying, swap them for themed sprites via search_library + generate_image (see assetHints.props / assetHints.backgrounds).
    - screens: 1
    - requires AIGC assets: no
    - visual prior: Portrait 9:16, 2D-over-camera-feed Christmas scene. Top edge: Christmas garland border (720×200px). Santa rig at upper-center: Santa parent at (0, +380), swings horizontally with sin pendulum (amplitude=240px, speed=2 rad/s). Children of Santa: rope (15×180px at local +160y), Santa body (120×140px), 3 gifts (60×60px each) stacked at local (0, -30) — Gift1 renders on top. Bottom third: 3 cartoon houses (180×160px) at x=-220, 0, +220 with widened chimneys (100×118px) at y=-168.96 sticking out behind each roof (chimney rendered behind house image so the lower 38px is hidden by the roof). Each house has an invisible chute formed by 2 BoxCollider2D walls at x ± 56 (height ~220px from y=-110 down to y=-340) plus an invisible HouseFloor collider at y=-340 (delivery trigger). 3 Social Kit Profile Photo friends (60×60px) sit on the front porch at (house_x, -310) with a Christmas hat child at local (-17, +36). 4 invisible ground-collider segments at y=-285 between the chute openings catch gifts that miss the chimney. Decorative tree at far left (-300, -310). HUD: Prompt text at (0, +200), Result text at (0, +120) hidden until endgame. 3 check sprites parked off-screen (x=2000+) until the script teleports the matching one to (house_x, -130) on delivery.
    - preview images: intro, early, near_win, won, lost (attached above when within the image cap — match them by the numbered legend)
    - **how to use**: tier=weak — loosely related, NOT an apply candidate. Do NOT apply. Borrow individual visual elements / layout / palette via `mechanic_refs` if they fit your design.

- **AR head control** (`ar_head_control`) — score 0.433
  - family: AR Head Control
  - gameplay: AR head-tilt character control: AR Head Tracker reads head pitch/yaw; tilting head moves a player character horizontally/vertically across a game area (player clamped within bounds). Obstacles or collectibles populate the game area; collisions with the player either deduct life or increment score (theme-dependent). HUD shows score. Themes: tilt-steer a vehicle, dodge falling obstacles by leaning, collect items by tilting.
  - tags: ar, head, tilt, nod, control, motion
  - **buildable** `ar_head_control`
    - description: AR camera with head tracking controlling player character
    - screens: 2
    - requires AIGC assets: no
    - **how to use**: tier=weak — loosely related, NOT an apply candidate. Do NOT apply. Borrow individual visual elements / layout / palette via `mechanic_refs` if they fit your design.

- **Collecting dodge** (`collecting_dodge`) — score 0.421
  - family: Collecting/Dodge
  - gameplay: Catch-and-dodge runner: items spawn at random horizontal positions and fall from the top of the screen at intervals. Player drags a character along the bottom to catch desirable items (score+) and dodge harmful items (life−). Round ends when lives hit 0. HUD shows score and remaining lives. Themes: rain catching, falling fruit, food fight.

- **AR face game** (`ar_face_game`) — score 0.376
  - family: AR Face Game
  - gameplay: AR face-expression challenge: AR Head Tracker reads the user's facial expressions (smile, mouth-open, eyebrow raise, blink) in real time. The game prompts a target expression; each match awards points. A decoration layer (mask/sticker) sits on the user's face for visual flair while playing. HUD shows score + current expression prompt. Round is time-limited; game-over when timer expires.
  - tags: ar, face, filter, mask, decoration, beauty

    - description: AR camera with face tracking, decorations, and game HUD
    - screens: 2

    - **how to use**: tier=weak — loosely related, NOT an apply candidate. Do NOT apply. Borrow individual visual elements / layout / palette via `mechanic_refs` if they fit your design.

- **Squirrel Acorn Balance** (`squirrel_acorn_balance`) — score 0.371
  - family: drop-balance-tilt
  - gameplay: A character holds a basket on a fulcrum/balance arm. Items (acorns) fall from above and land in the basket; each added item shifts the basket's tilt left or right depending on landing position. Player taps left or right (or tilts head) to nudge the balance back toward center. A horizontal tilt-meter shows the current angle with a safe zone in the middle. Lose if the tilt indicator exits the safe zone (basket spills); goal is to survive as long as possible while items keep falling.
  - tags: balance, tilt, drop, physics, basket, squirrel, acorn, left, right, meter, casual
